prompt: Patrick has a leprechaun hat that looks like a tall, green top hat. The main portion of the hat is a cylinder that is 8 inches tall and has a 3-inch radius. He will fill this portion of the hat with chocolates wrapped to resemble small gold coins to pass out to all his friends. One bag of these chocolate "coins" takes up about 20 in³ of space. What is the minimum number of bags of chocolate that Patrick must get to completely fill his hat?

solutions.title: Volume, then divide
solutions.body:
$V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(3^2)(8) = 72\pi \approx 226.2$ in³. Bags: $226.2 \div 20 \approx 11.3$, so 11 bags aren't enough; he needs **12**.

**Answer: 12 bags**

solutions.title: Compare with 11 and 12 bags
solutions.body:
11 bags fill $220$ in³ and 12 bags fill $240$ in³. Since $72\pi \approx 226$ is between them, 12 bags are needed.

**Answer: 12 bags**

prompt: Margaret painted a mural for St. Patrick's Day and mixed her own green paint. She mixed 3 parts yellow paint with 2 parts blue paint to create green paint. Maureen wanted to also paint a mural with the same green color, but she currently has 8 cups of green paint that is a mixture of 40% yellow paint and 60% blue paint. To get the same shade of green as Margaret, how many cups of yellow paint must she add to her mixture?

solutions.title: Set up a proportion
solutions.body:
Maureen has $0.4 \times 8 = 3.2$ cups yellow and $0.6 \times 8 = 4.8$ cups blue. Adding $x$ cups yellow: $\frac{3.2 + x}{4.8} = \frac32$, so $3.2 + x = 7.2$ and $x = 4$.

**Answer: 4 cups**

solutions.title: Blue stays fixed
solutions.body:
Blue is 2 parts and there are 4.8 cups of it, so 1 part $= 2.4$ cups. Yellow should be 3 parts $= 7.2$ cups. She has 3.2 cups, so she adds $7.2 - 3.2 = 4$ cups.

**Answer: 4 cups**

prompt: How many ways can we arrange the five letters in the word GREEN, even if they don't form real words, if any arrangement must keep the two Es together?

solutions.title: Glue the Es
solutions.body:
Treat EE as one block. Then we arrange 4 distinct items: G, R, N, [EE]. That gives $4! = 24$ arrangements (swapping the two identical Es gives nothing new).

**Answer: 24**

solutions.title: Place the EE block
solutions.body:
The EE block can start in position 1, 2, 3 or 4 (4 choices). The other three distinct letters fill the remaining 3 spots in $3! = 6$ ways: $4 \times 6 = 24$.

**Answer: 24**
